title: End Suction Centrifugal Pump

introduction.definition: An end suction centrifugal pump is a single-stage overhung pump in which liquid enters axially at one end of the casing, is accelerated by a rotating impeller and is collected by a volute that converts velocity into pressure. The frame-mounted back-pull-out version (API 610 OH1, ISO 2858, ASME B73.1) lets the rotating assembly be removed without disturbing the piping.
applications: Chemical and process transfer (ANSI/ISO process pumps)
Cooling and service water in plants
Alumina refinery liquor and utility services (clean or lightly contaminated liquids)
key_points: Most common pump type in industry
Single impeller, overhung on its bearings
Back pull-out: service without breaking pipe joints
Best efficiency near the BEP; operate within the preferred operating region

classification.configuration: Overhung, end suction, frame-mounted, foot-mounted casing
classification.dimensional_standards: ISO 2858 / ASME B73.1 (chemical process) or EN 733 (water)

introduction.summary: The end suction pump is the most widely used centrifugal pump. Liquid enters axially into the eye of a single impeller, is accelerated outward by the rotating vanes, and is collected by a spiral volute that converts velocity into pressure before leaving through the top discharge nozzle. In the frame-mounted, back-pull-out design (API 610 OH1, ISO 2858 / ASME B73.1), the impeller, seal, bearing frame and shaft can be withdrawn towards the motor as one unit, using a spacer coupling, without disturbing the casing or the pipework.

what_to_look_for: Liquid enters the suction nozzle axially and reaches the eye of the impeller at low pressure.
The rotating impeller vanes accelerate the liquid outward, giving it kinetic energy and some pressure rise.
Wear rings keep the clearance between the rotating impeller and the casing small, limiting leakage from discharge back to suction.

steps.text: Liquid enters the suction nozzle axially and reaches the eye of the impeller at low pressure.
The rotating impeller vanes accelerate the liquid outward, giving it kinetic energy and some pressure rise.
Wear rings keep the clearance between the rotating impeller and the casing small, limiting leakage from discharge back to suction.
The volute collects the liquid around the impeller and slows it gradually, converting velocity into pressure before the discharge nozzle.
The mechanical seal stops leakage where the shaft passes through the casing cover.
The bearing frame carries the radial load and the residual axial thrust; balance holes in the impeller reduce that thrust.
The motor drives the pump through a spacer coupling, which can be removed for back pull-out maintenance.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Head falls steadily as flow increases (stable, drooping-free curve for most designs); power rises with flow; efficiency peaks at the BEP; NPSHr rises at high flow.

parts.name: Volute Casing (Axial Suction, Top Discharge)
parts.function: Collects flow leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure in a spiral passage of increasing area, then discharges through a diffuser nozzle.
parts.material: Cast iron, ductile iron, carbon steel, stainless steel (CF8M), duplex.

parts.name: Casing Wear Rings (Front & Back)
parts.function: Renewable close-clearance ring that limits recirculation from discharge back to suction.
parts.material: Bronze, cast iron, hardened stainless steel; dissimilar hardness to avoid galling.

parts.name: Closed Impeller (6 vanes, balance holes)
parts.function: Adds energy to the liquid; blades between hub and shrouds accelerate the liquid outward.
parts.material: Cast iron, bronze, stainless steel (CF8M, CA6NM), duplex.

parts.name: Casing Cover & Seal Chamber
parts.function: Closes the back of the casing and forms the seal chamber.

parts.name: Cartridge Mechanical Seal
parts.function: Seals the rotating shaft where it leaves the pressurised casing.
parts.material: Faces: carbon-graphite, silicon carbide, tungsten carbide; metal parts stainless steel; elastomers per fluid.

parts.name: Bearing Frame
parts.function: Holds the shaft bearings and oil or grease, and supports the overhung impeller.

parts.name: Radial Bearing (Inboard)
parts.function: Carries radial load near the impeller end.

parts.name: Thrust Bearings (Duplex Angular-Contact, Outboard)
parts.function: Carries axial hydraulic thrust and locates the shaft axially.
parts.material: Bearing steel; brass or polyamide cages.

parts.name: Pump Shaft
parts.function: Transmits torque from the coupling to the impeller(s).
parts.material: Carbon steel, 4140 alloy steel, 410/420 or 316 stainless, duplex.

parts.name: Flexible Coupling
parts.function: Transmits torque between motor and pump while accommodating small misalignment and allowing separation for maintenance.
parts.material: Steel or cast iron hubs; elastomer or stainless-steel disc elements.

parts.name: Coupling Guard
parts.material: Steel, aluminium or non-sparking brass for hazardous areas.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Frame & End Shields
parts.function: Encloses the stator and supports the bearings; feet or flange mount the motor to the baseplate or pump.
parts.material: Cast iron or aluminium frame; steel fasteners.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Stator
parts.material: Silicon electrical steel, copper magnet wire, Class F/H insulation (typical).

parts.name: Electric Motor – Rotor & Shaft
parts.function: Converts the rotating field into shaft torque (squirrel-cage induction rotor).
parts.material: Electrical steel, die-cast aluminium or copper.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Bearings (DE & NDE)
parts.function: Support the motor rotor at drive and non-drive ends.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Cooling Fan
parts.function: Draws cooling air over the finned frame.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Fan Cover
parts.function: Guards the fan and directs air along the fins.

parts.name: Baseplate
parts.function: Provides a rigid common mounting for pump and driver, maintains alignment and transfers loads to the foundation.
parts.material: Carbon steel, painted; stainless steel for hygienic or corrosive areas.

parts.name: Suction & Discharge Pressure Gauges
parts.function: Indicates suction or discharge pressure for operation and performance checks.
parts.material: Stainless steel case and wetted parts.

engineering_parameters.basis: Typical published range for this design class (not a rating of the 3-D model or of any specific product). Verify against the selected manufacturer datasheet and performance curve; fill reference_model when a specific product is chosen.

flow.note: Larger sizes exist; ISO 2858 covers up to about 400 m³/h at its nominal duty points.

head.note: Single stage; up to ~220 m for large two-pole process pumps.

pressure.note: ISO 2858 is a PN16 standard; ASME B73.1 ductile/steel casings ~ class 150/300 flange ratings.

efficiency.note: Rises with pump size and with specific speed up to the optimum (Ns ≈ 2,000–3,000 US units).

selection_notes: Select so the duty point lies at 80–110 % of BEP flow.
Check NPSH margin (NPSHa ≥ NPSHr × margin, ANSI/HI 9.6.1).
Choose casing material and seal plan from the liquid and temperature.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, grouted baseplate on a concrete foundation of about 3–5× the mass of the unit (rule of thumb — verify with the manufacturer).
Level the baseplate to the manufacturer's tolerance before grouting; use epoxy or non-shrink grout with no voids.
alignment: Align pump and motor shafts with dial indicators or laser after grouting and again after connecting the piping (hot alignment check for hot service).
Target the coupling manufacturer's tolerances; typical practice for 1500–3000 rpm is ≤0.05 mm offset and ≤0.05 mm/100 mm angularity — verify.
Correct soft foot (< 0.05 mm) before final alignment.
piping: Support suction and discharge piping independently so nozzle loads stay within the manufacturer's (or API 610/HI 9.6.2) allowable values.
Provide a straight run of at least 5 pipe diameters ahead of the suction nozzle (ANSI/HI 9.6.6 guidance — verify) and use an eccentric reducer with the flat side up.
Fit isolation valves on both sides, a check valve on the discharge, and pressure gauges at suction and discharge.
Never use the pump as a pipe anchor; use expansion joints with tie rods only when designed for them.
commissioning: Fill and vent the casing; never run dry.
Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Start against a partly open discharge valve, then open to the duty point; avoid running at shut-off.
Record baseline vibration, bearing temperature, suction and discharge pressure, flow and motor current.
Confirm the seal flush plan is connected and working before start-up.

routine.task: Check bearing temperature, vibration and noise.
Inspect the mechanical seal for leakage.
Check suction and discharge pressure against the baseline.

periodic.task: Change the bearing-frame oil (or regrease) at the interval in the manual.
Check coupling alignment and the condition of the coupling elements.

overhaul.task: Pull out the rotating assembly; measure wear-ring clearance and replace rings when clearance reaches about twice the new value.
Inspect the impeller for cavitation and erosion; check the shaft run-out and the seal faces.

lubrication: Oil-bath or oil-mist lubrication: keep the oil level at the sight-glass mark; use the ISO VG grade specified (often VG 46/68).
Grease-lubricated bearings: do not over-grease — follow the quantity and interval in the manual.

causes: NPSHa too low (high suction lift, hot liquid, clogged strainer)
remedies: Raise suction level or reduce suction losses

symptoms: Visible drips or spray at the seal
causes: Wrong seal plan or worn faces

symptoms: Rising overall vibration at 1× or 2× running speed
remedies: Move duty to the preferred operating region

symptoms: Noise, vibration at bearing defect frequencies
causes: Excess axial thrust from worn wear rings

script.narration: This module introduces the End Suction Centrifugal Pump.

An end suction centrifugal pump is a single-stage overhung pump in which liquid enters axially at one end of the casing, is accelerated by a rotating impeller and is collected by a volute that converts velocity into pressure.
The frame-mounted back-pull-out version (API 610 OH1, ISO 2858, ASME B73.1) lets the rotating assembly be removed without disturbing the piping.
Typical applications include water supply and distribution; HVAC chilled and condenser water; chemical and process transfer (ANSI/ISO process pumps); cooling and service water in plants.

video_tutorials.title: End Suction Centrifugal Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the End Suction Centrifugal Pump.
Check bearing temperature, vibration and noise.
Inspect the mechanical seal for leakage.
Check suction and discharge pressure against the baseline.
Change the bearing-frame oil (or regrease) at the interval in the manual.
Check coupling alignment and the condition of the coupling elements.
Pull out the rotating assembly; measure wear-ring clearance and replace rings when clearance reaches about twice the new value.
Inspect the impeller for cavitation and erosion; check the shaft run-out and the seal faces.
Watch for cavitation: crackling noise like gravel. Common cause: npsha too low (high suction lift, hot liquid, clogged strainer).
Watch for seal leakage: visible drips or spray at the seal. Common cause: dry running.
Watch for high vibration: rising overall vibration at 1× or 2× running speed. Common cause: misalignment.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: In a back-pull-out end suction pump, what can be removed without disconnecting the suction and discharge piping?
options: The complete rotating assembly (impeller, seal, bearing frame)
Nothing — the casing must be removed first
questions.explanation: The casing stays bolted to the pipework; the rotating assembly is withdrawn towards the motor after removing the spacer.

questions.question: Which component converts most of the liquid's velocity into pressure?
questions.explanation: The impeller adds energy; the expanding volute slows the flow and converts kinetic energy into pressure.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the wear rings?
options: Limit leakage from discharge back to the impeller eye
questions.explanation: A small running clearance limits internal recirculation; as it wears, efficiency drops.

questions.question: Where should the operating point ideally be on the curve?
questions.explanation: Near BEP the radial loads, vibration and recirculation are lowest and efficiency is highest.

questions.question: Cavitation occurs when…
options: NPSH available is less than NPSH required
questions.explanation: If the suction pressure falls to vapour pressure at the impeller eye, vapour bubbles form and collapse, damaging the vanes.

questions.question: Which API 610 type code designates a foot-mounted, horizontal overhung pump?
Which component has this function? "Collects flow leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure in a spiral passage of increasing area, then discharges through a diffuser nozzle."
questions.explanation: Volute Casing (Axial Suction, Top Discharge): Collects flow leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure in a spiral passage of increasing area, then discharges through a diffuser nozzle.

questions.question: Which component has this function? "Renewable close-clearance ring that limits recirculation from discharge back to suction."
questions.explanation: Casing Wear Rings (Front & Back): Renewable close-clearance ring that limits recirculation from discharge back to suction.
